  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend csec ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(date -u -d "$cstart" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        ce=$(date -u -d "$cend" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."
            else
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — below the ceiling; check the run timeline for a whole-run cancellation before treating this as a leg defect."
            fi
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN
  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),
  # the root cause is already tracked: comment there with the new run link
  # instead of filing a symptom duplicate that re-fires every day.
  if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
    local sigmatch
    sigmatch=$(find_issue_by_signature "$sig")
    if [ -n "$sigmatch" ]; then
      {
        echo "**Root-cause dedup (gh-1478):** this failure's error signature matches #$sigmatch — the digest below is a fresh data point for that issue, not a new bug."
        echo
        cat "$body"
      } > "$body.sig"
      gh issue comment "$sigmatch" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body.sig" >/dev/null
      actions+="updated #${sigmatch} ($leg — signature matches an open root cause)"$'\n'
      rm -f "$body" "$body.sig"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'
  else

      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then

      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$body"

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature$
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code$
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,$
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) M-bM-^@M-^T the dedup$
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).$
  awk '$
    {$
      pr = 0$

      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2$
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3$
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4$
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5$
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }$
    }$
    END { if (best) print sig }' \$

{"newText":"log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2

{"newText":"log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    index($0, "name: .Leg: " frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.

    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.

      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend csec ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")

        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"

        local cs="" ce=""

        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))

        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),
  # the root cause is already tracked: comment there with the new run link
  # instead of filing a symptom duplicate that re-fires every day.
  if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
    local sigmatch
    sigmatch=$(find_issue_by_signature "$sig")
    if [ -n "$sigmatch" ]; then
      {
        echo "**Root-cause dedup (gh-1478):** this failure's error signature matches #$sigmatch — the digest below is a fresh data point for that issue, not a new bug."
        echo
        cat "$body"
      } > "$body.sig"
      gh issue comment "$sigmatch" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body.sig" >/dev/null
      actions+="updated #${sigmatch} ($leg — signature matches an open root cause)"$'\n'
      rm -f "$body" "$body.sig"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'

    created=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body-file "$body" \
      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then
      actions+="filed ${created} ($leg failed)"$'\n'
    else
      echo "::warning::could not file the self-healing issue for leg '$leg' (permissions?)"
      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$body"

{"newText":"log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    index($0, "name: .Leg: " frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi

{"newText":"file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend csec ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(date -u -d "$cstart" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        ce=$(date -u -d "$cend" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."
            else
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — below the ceiling; check the run timeline for a whole-run cancellation before treating this as a leg defect."
            fi
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"

}$

{"newText":"log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    index($0, "name: .Leg: " frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi

{"newText":"file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend csec ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(date -u -d "$cstart" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        ce=$(date -u -d "$cend" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."
            else
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — below the ceiling; check the run timeline for a whole-run cancellation before treating this as a leg defect."
            fi
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN
  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),
  # the root cause is already tracked: comment there with the new run link
  # instead of filing a symptom duplicate that re-fires every day.
  if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
    local sigmatch
    sigmatch=$(find_issue_by_signature "$sig")
    if [ -n "$sigmatch" ]; then
      {
        echo "**Root-cause dedup (gh-1478):** this failure's error signature matches #$sigmatch — the digest below is a fresh data point for that issue, not a new bug."
        echo
        cat "$body"
      } > "$body.sig"
      gh issue comment "$sigmatch" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body.sig" >/dev/null
      actions+="updated #${sigmatch} ($leg — signature matches an open root cause)"$'\n'
      rm -f "$body" "$body.sig"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'
  else
    local created
    created=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body-file "$body" \
      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then
      actions+="filed ${created} ($leg failed)"$'\n'
    else
      echo "::warning::could not file the self-healing issue for leg '$leg' (permissions?)"
      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$body"

# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'$
  # bodies AND comments M-bM-^@M-^T a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so$
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.$
  local q$
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \$
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \$
      | cut -c1-200)$
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0$
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \$
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \$
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true$
}$

Bash comments don't start mid-word... wait, this IS a full-line comment starting with `#`. Bash ignores quotes in comments. Hmm wait, no! The problem is different. Look at line 144: it's a comment, fine. But wait — is it? The tokenizer... full-line `#` comment — quotes ignored. So why does head -149 complain about matching `'` at line 149?

Line 149: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — wait, the second quote: `' \` — that's quote-space-backslash... the `' '` closes, then ` \`?? No wait: `'[:alnum:]./+-'` then space then `' '` then... the line shows `' \` at end — that's `'` SPACE `\`. So the second single-quoted argument is `' '` — open quote, space, close quote — then a space, then backslash continuation. Balanced!

Hmm, but count quotes on line 149: characters: ' [ : a l p h a n u m : ] . / + - '  → 2; then ' → 3rd, space, ' → wait `' \` is only ONE quote! Look: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$` — after `'[:alnum:]./+-'` there's ` '` then ` \`. So we have THREE quotes on the line: open `[...]`, close after `+-`, open before space... and the closing quote is MISSING — the `\` came right after the space inside... no wait: `' \$` = quote, space, backslash, end. So third quote OPENS and never closes on this line — it continues to the NEXT line! The next line `      | sed -e 's/^ *//' ...` — the continued quote swallows `| sed -e ` until the next `'` which is the opening of `'s/^ *//'`... that CLOSES the string instead of opening! Chaos.

The bug: I intended `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' '` with a line continuation. {"newText":"log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    index($0, "name: .Leg: " frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi

  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend csec ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(date -u -d "$cstart" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        ce=$(date -u -d "$cend" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."

            fi

        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN
  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),
  # the root cause is already tracked: comment there with the new run link
  # instead of filing a symptom duplicate that re-fires every day.
  if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
    local sigmatch
    sigmatch=$(find_issue_by_signature "$sig")
    if [ -n "$sigmatch" ]; then
      {
        echo "**Root-cause dedup (gh-1478):** this failure's error signature matches #$sigmatch — the digest below is a fresh data point for that issue, not a new bug."
        echo
        cat "$body"
      } > "$body.sig"
      gh issue comment "$sigmatch" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body.sig" >/dev/null
      actions+="updated #${sigmatch} ($leg — signature matches an open root cause)"$'\n'
      rm -f "$body" "$body.sig"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'

      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)

      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi

# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'$
  # bodies AND comments M-bM-^@M-^T a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so$
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.$
  local q$
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \$
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \$
      | cut -c1-200)$
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0$
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \$
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \$
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true$
}$
$

Hmm wait, no! The problem is different. Look at line 144: it's a comment, fine. But wait — is it? The tokenizer... full-line `#` comment — quotes ignored. So why does head -149 complain about matching `'` at line 149?

Line 149: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — wait, the second quote: `' \` — that's quote-space-backslash... the `' '` closes, then ` \`?? No wait: `'[:alnum:]./+-'` then space then `' '` then... the line shows `' \` at end — that's `'` SPACE `\`. So the second single-quoted argument is `' '` — open quote, space, close quote — then a space, then backslash continuation. Balanced!

Hmm, but count quotes on line 149: characters: ' [ : a l p h a n u m : ] . / + - '  → 2; then ' → 3rd, space, ' → wait `' \` is only ONE quote! Look: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$` — after `'[:alnum:]./+-'` there's ` '` then ` \`. So we have THREE quotes on the line: open `[...]`, close after `+-`, open before space... and the closing quote is MISSING — the `\` came right after the space inside... no wait: `' \$` = quote, space, backslash, end. The next line `      | sed -e 's/^ *//' ...` — the continued quote swallows `| sed -e ` until the next `'` which is the opening of `'s/^ *//'`... that CLOSES the string instead of opening! Chaos.

{"newText":"log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    index($0, "name: .Leg: " frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}","oldText":"log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix

{"newText":"file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend csec ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(date -u -d "$cstart" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        ce=$(date -u -d "$cend" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."
            else
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — below the ceiling; check the run timeline for a whole-run cancellation before treating this as a leg defect."
            fi
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN
  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),
  # the root cause is already tracked: comment there with the new run link
  # instead of filing a symptom duplicate that re-fires every day.
  if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
    local sigmatch
    sigmatch=$(find_issue_by_signature "$sig")
    if [ -n "$sigmatch" ]; then
      {
        echo "**Root-cause dedup (gh-1478):** this failure's error signature matches #$sigmatch — the digest below is a fresh data point for that issue, not a new bug."
        echo
        cat "$body"
      } > "$body.sig"
      gh issue comment "$sigmatch" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body.sig" >/dev/null
      actions+="updated #${sigmatch} ($leg — signature matches an open root cause)"$'\n'
      rm -f "$body" "$body.sig"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'
  else
    local created
    created=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body-file "$body" \
      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then
      actions+="filed ${created} ($leg failed)"$'\n'
    else
      echo "::warning::could not file the self-healing issue for leg '$leg' (permissions?)"
      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$body"
}","oldText":"file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result

  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"

  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."

      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend csec ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(date -u -d "$cstart" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        ce=$(date -u -d "$cend" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."
            else
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — below the ceiling; check the run timeline for a whole-run cancellation before treating this as a leg defect."
            fi

        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN
  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),
  # the root cause is already tracked: comment there with the new run link
  # instead of filing a symptom duplicate that re-fires every day.
  if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
    local sigmatch
    sigmatch=$(find_issue_by_signature "$sig")
    if [ -n "$sigmatch" ]; then
      {
        echo "**Root-cause dedup (gh-1478):** this failure's error signature matches #$sigmatch — the digest below is a fresh data point for that issue, not a new bug."
        echo
        cat "$body"
      } > "$body.sig"
      gh issue comment "$sigmatch" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body.sig" >/dev/null
      actions+="updated #${sigmatch} ($leg — signature matches an open root cause)"$'\n'
      rm -f "$body" "$body.sig"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'

    created=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body-file "$body" \
      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then
      actions+="filed ${created} ($leg failed)"$'\n'
    else
      echo "::warning::could not file the self-healing issue for leg '$leg' (permissions?)"
      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi

# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'$
  # bodies AND comments M-bM-^@M-^T a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so$
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.$
  local q$
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \$
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \$
      | cut -c1-200)$
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0$
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \$
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \$
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true$
}$
$

blocks.text:
Line 144: `# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'` — the COMMENT contains an apostrophe: "issues'". Bash comments don't start mid-word... wait, this IS a full-line comment starting with `#`. Bash ignores quotes in comments. BUT — the problem: this comment is INSIDE the function `find_issue_by_signature`, and the apostrophe is harmless in a comment...

Hmm wait, no! The problem is different. Look at line 144: it's a comment, fine. But wait — is it? The tokenizer... full-line `#` comment — quotes ignored. So why does head -149 complain about matching `'` at line 149?

Line 149: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — wait, the second quote: `' \` — that's quote-space-backslash... the `' '` closes, then ` \`?? No wait: `'[:alnum:]./+-'` then space then `' '` then... the line shows `' \` at end — that's `'` SPACE `\`. So the second single-quoted argument is `' '` — open quote, space, close quote — then a space, then backslash continuation. Balanced!

Hmm, but count quotes on line 149: characters: ' [ : a l p h a n u m : ] . / + - '  → 2; then ' → 3rd, space, ' → wait `' \` is only ONE quote! Look: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$` — after `'[:alnum:]./+-'` there's ` '` then ` \`. So we have THREE quotes on the line: open `[...]`, close after `+-`, open before space... and the closing quote is MISSING — the `\` came right after the space inside... no wait: `' \$` = quote, space, backslash, end. So third quote OPENS and never closes on this line — it continues to the NEXT line! The next line `      | sed -e 's/^ *//' ...` — the continued quote swallows `| sed -e ` until the next `'` which is the opening of `'s/^ *//'`... that CLOSES the string instead of opening! Chaos.

The bug: I intended `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' '` with a line continuation. The closing `'` of the second arg got lost — in my edit I wrote `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — the `' '` was meant to be quote-space-quote but became quote-space. Fix: put a literal closing quote: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \`.

Wait, actually looking at my edit text: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — yes I wrote `' '` incorrectly as `' \`. Fix it.
Found it — line 149: the second `tr` argument lost its closing quote (`' \` should be `' ' \`):

# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'$
  # bodies AND comments M-bM-^@M-^T a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so$
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.$
  local q$
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \$
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \$
      | cut -c1-200)$
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0$
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \$
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \$
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true$
}$
$

Line 144: `# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'` — the COMMENT contains an apostrophe: "issues'". Bash comments don't start mid-word... wait, this IS a full-line comment starting with `#`. Bash ignores quotes in comments. BUT — the problem: this comment is INSIDE the function `find_issue_by_signature`, and the apostrophe is harmless in a comment...

Hmm wait, no! The problem is different. Look at line 144: it's a comment, fine. But wait — is it? The tokenizer... full-line `#` comment — quotes ignored. So why does head -149 complain about matching `'` at line 149?

Line 149: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — wait, the second quote: `' \` — that's quote-space-backslash... the `' '` closes, then ` \`?? No wait: `'[:alnum:]./+-'` then space then `' '` then... the line shows `' \` at end — that's `'` SPACE `\`. So the second single-quoted argument is `' '` — open quote, space, close quote — then a space, then backslash continuation. Balanced!

Hmm, but count quotes on line 149: characters: ' [ : a l p h a n u m : ] . / + - '  → 2; then ' → 3rd, space, ' → wait `' \` is only ONE quote! Look: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$` — after `'[:alnum:]./+-'` there's ` '` then ` \`. So we have THREE quotes on the line: open `[...]`, close after `+-`, open before space... and the closing quote is MISSING — the `\` came right after the space inside... no wait: `' \$` = quote, space, backslash, end. So third quote OPENS and never closes on this line — it continues to the NEXT line! The next line `      | sed -e 's/^ *//' ...` — the continued quote swallows `| sed -e ` until the next `'` which is the opening of `'s/^ *//'`... that CLOSES the string instead of opening! Chaos.

The bug: I intended `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' '` with a line continuation. The closing `'` of the second arg got lost — in my edit I wrote `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — the `' '` was meant to be quote-space-quote but became quote-space. Fix: put a literal closing quote: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \`.

Also update the reason text "05:17:00Z -> 11:16:53Z elapsed" stays fine. Now the workflow verify step. Add after the report step in daily-publish.yml:

```yaml
      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        ...
        run: bash scripts/daily_publish_report.sh

      # gh-1478: the inject_failure TEST hook must prove the digest QUOTES the
      # injected ::error:: line (signal-first excerpt), not merely that an
      # issue was filed — the #1473 tree-noise regression class.
      - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)
        if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
        env:
          INJECTED: ${{ inputs.inject_failure }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed"
          n=$(gh issue list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --state open \
                --label daily-publish --limit 200 \
                --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' \
                | while IFS=$'\t' read -r num t; do
                    [ "$t" = "$title" ] && echo "$num"
                  done | head -1)
          if [ -z "$n" ]; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: no open issue titled '${title}' — the self-filing path regressed"
            exit 1
          fi
          text=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
                   --json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)')
          if ! grep -qF "injected failure (inject_failure=${INJECTED})" <<< "$text"; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: issue #${n} never quotes the injected ::error:: line — the signal-first excerpt regressed (gh-1478)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "inject_failure verify OK: issue #${n} quotes the injected error line (gh-1478)"
```

Note: the marker in the body — the issue body contains the excerpt with the injected line. grep -qF fixed string. Good.

The verify step runs even when the report step failed (`always()`), but if the report job's earlier step failed (checkout), the step still runs and fails with "no open issue" — acceptable for a TEST-only hook (workflow_dispatch only).

```yaml

      - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)
        if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
        env:
          INJECTED: ${{ inputs.inject_failure }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed"
          n=$(gh issue list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --state open \
                --label daily-publish --limit 200 \
                --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' \
                | while IFS=$'\t' read -r num t; do
                    [ "$t" = "$title" ] && echo "$num"
                  done | head -1)
          if [ -z "$n" ]; then

Hmm wait, no! The problem is different. Look at line 144: it's a comment, fine. But wait — is it? The tokenizer... full-line `#` comment — quotes ignored. So why does head -149 complain about matching `'` at line 149?

Line 149: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — wait, the second quote: `' \` — that's quote-space-backslash... the `' '` closes, then ` \`?? No wait: `'[:alnum:]./+-'` then space then `' '` then... the line shows `' \` at end — that's `'` SPACE `\`. So the second single-quoted argument is `' '` — open quote, space, close quote — then a space, then backslash continuation. Balanced!

Hmm, but count quotes on line 149: characters: ' [ : a l p h a n u m : ] . / + - '  → 2; then ' → 3rd, space, ' → wait `' \` is only ONE quote! Look: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$` — after `'[:alnum:]./+-'` there's ` '` then ` \`. So we have THREE quotes on the line: open `[...]`, close after `+-`, open before space... and the closing quote is MISSING — the `\` came right after the space inside... no wait: `' \$` = quote, space, backslash, end. So third quote OPENS and never closes on this line — it continues to the NEXT line! The next line `      | sed -e 's/^ *//' ...` — the continued quote swallows `| sed -e ` until the next `'` which is the opening of `'s/^ *//'`... that CLOSES the string instead of opening! Chaos.

        if (++hits <= 3)$

        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]$

# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'$
  # bodies AND comments M-bM-^@M-^T a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so$
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.$

    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \$

Hmm wait, no! The problem is different. Look at line 144: it's a comment, fine. But wait — is it? The tokenizer... full-line `#` comment — quotes ignored. So why does head -149 complain about matching `'` at line 149?

Line 149: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — wait, the second quote: `' \` — that's quote-space-backslash... the `' '` closes, then ` \`?? No wait: `'[:alnum:]./+-'` then space then `' '` then... the line shows `' \` at end — that's `'` SPACE `\`. So the second single-quoted argument is `' '` — open quote, space, close quote — then a space, then backslash continuation. Balanced!

Hmm, but count quotes on line 149: characters: ' [ : a l p h a n u m : ] . / + - '  → 2; then ' → 3rd, space, ' → wait `' \` is only ONE quote! Look: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$` — after `'[:alnum:]./+-'` there's ` '` then ` \`. So we have THREE quotes on the line: open `[...]`, close after `+-`, open before space... and the closing quote is MISSING — the `\` came right after the space inside... no wait: `' \$` = quote, space, backslash, end. So third quote OPENS and never closes on this line — it continues to the NEXT line! The next line `      | sed -e 's/^ *//' ...` — the continued quote swallows `| sed -e ` until the next `'` which is the opening of `'s/^ *//'`... that CLOSES the string instead of opening! Chaos.
