Line 144: `# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'` — the COMMENT contains an apostrophe: "issues'". Bash comments don't start mid-word... wait, this IS a full-line comment starting with `#`. Bash ignores quotes in comments. BUT — the problem: this comment is INSIDE the function `find_issue_by_signature`, and the apostrophe is harmless in a comment...

Hmm wait, no! The problem is different. Look at line 144: it's a comment, fine. But wait — is it? The tokenizer... full-line `#` comment — quotes ignored. So why does head -149 complain about matching `'` at line 149?

Line 149: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — wait, the second quote: `' \` — that's quote-space-backslash... the `' '` closes, then ` \`?? No wait: `'[:alnum:]./+-'` then space then `' '` then... the line shows `' \` at end — that's `'` SPACE `\`. So the second single-quoted argument is `' '` — open quote, space, close quote — then a space, then backslash continuation. Balanced!

Hmm, but count quotes on line 149: characters: ' [ : a l p h a n u m : ] . / + - '  → 2; then ' → 3rd, space, ' → wait `' \` is only ONE quote! Look: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$` — after `'[:alnum:]./+-'` there's ` '` then ` \`. So we have THREE quotes on the line: open `[...]`, close after `+-`, open before space... and the closing quote is MISSING — the `\` came right after the space inside... no wait: `' \$` = quote, space, backslash, end. So third quote OPENS and never closes on this line — it continues to the NEXT line! The next line `      | sed -e 's/^ *//' ...` — the continued quote swallows `| sed -e ` until the next `'` which is the opening of `'s/^ *//'`... that CLOSES the string instead of opening! Chaos.

The bug: I intended `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' '` with a line continuation. The closing `'` of the second arg got lost — in my edit I wrote `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — the `' '` was meant to be quote-space-quote but became quote-space. Fix: put a literal closing quote: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \`.

# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'$
  # bodies AND comments M-bM-^@M-^T a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so$
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.$
  local q$

      | cut -c1-200)$
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0$
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \$
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \$
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true$
}$

blocks.text:
Line 144: `# gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'` — the COMMENT contains an apostrophe: "issues'". Bash comments don't start mid-word... wait, this IS a full-line comment starting with `#`. Bash ignores quotes in comments. BUT — the problem: this comment is INSIDE the function `find_issue_by_signature`, and the apostrophe is harmless in a comment...

Hmm wait, no! The problem is different. Look at line 144: it's a comment, fine. But wait — is it? The tokenizer... full-line `#` comment — quotes ignored. So why does head -149 complain about matching `'` at line 149?

Line 149: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — wait, the second quote: `' \` — that's quote-space-backslash... the `' '` closes, then ` \`?? No wait: `'[:alnum:]./+-'` then space then `' '` then... the line shows `' \` at end — that's `'` SPACE `\`. So the second single-quoted argument is `' '` — open quote, space, close quote — then a space, then backslash continuation. Balanced!

Hmm, but count quotes on line 149: characters: ' [ : a l p h a n u m : ] . / + - '  → 2; then ' → 3rd, space, ' → wait `' \` is only ONE quote! Look: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$` — after `'[:alnum:]./+-'` there's ` '` then ` \`. So we have THREE quotes on the line: open `[...]`, close after `+-`, open before space... and the closing quote is MISSING — the `\` came right after the space inside... no wait: `' \$` = quote, space, backslash, end. So third quote OPENS and never closes on this line — it continues to the NEXT line! The next line `      | sed -e 's/^ *//' ...` — the continued quote swallows `| sed -e ` until the next `'` which is the opening of `'s/^ *//'`... that CLOSES the string instead of opening! Chaos.

The bug: I intended `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' '` with a line continuation. The closing `'` of the second arg got lost — in my edit I wrote `tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — the `' '` was meant to be quote-space-quote but became quote-space. Fix: put a literal closing quote: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \`.

Wait, actually looking at my edit text: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — yes I wrote `' '` incorrectly as `' \`. Fix it.

Hmm wait, no! The problem is different. Look at line 144: it's a comment, fine. But wait — is it? The tokenizer... full-line `#` comment — quotes ignored. So why does head -149 complain about matching `'` at line 149?

Line 149: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \` — wait, the second quote: `' \` — that's quote-space-backslash... the `' '` closes, then ` \`?? No wait: `'[:alnum:]./+-'` then space then `' '` then... the line shows `' \` at end — that's `'` SPACE `\`. So the second single-quoted argument is `' '` — open quote, space, close quote — then a space, then backslash continuation. Balanced!

Hmm, but count quotes on line 149: characters: ' [ : a l p h a n u m : ] . / + - '  → 2; then ' → 3rd, space, ' → wait `' \` is only ONE quote! Look: `| tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' \$` — after `'[:alnum:]./+-'` there's ` '` then ` \`.       - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)

# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>…

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing

# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>…

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do

}

# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>…

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"

`index(h, "name: .")` returns 0?! But `index(h, "name: ")` = 5 and haystack has "name: 'Leg". The pattern "name: ." should match at 5: "name: " followed by any char ('). index() treats the second arg as a LITERAL string, not regex! "name: ." as a literal requires a literal "." character! Of course! index() is literal substring — the `.` doesn't match the quote.

Fix: use a different approach — match either quote: since I can't know the quote char, use two index checks or use regex match():

```awk
$0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { ... }
```

Dynamic regex via string concatenation in ~ — supported in gawk/posix? `~` with a string expression is POSIX (dynamic regex). The frag may contain regex metachars: "Leg: pub.dev" — "." in pub.dev would match any char — harmless (still matches). "+" in "CLI + macOS" — literal "+" in ERE is fine ("+" alone is not special). blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m

  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \

# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>…

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing

  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q

      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \

    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing

  awk '

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing

  local q

      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do

}

# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>…

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend csec ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(date -u -d "$cstart" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        ce=$(date -u -d "$cend" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then

              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"

      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line

    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"

  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

arguments.content:
### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart
```
Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10089 passed, 10 skipped.

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[Failed/cancelled leg] --> FS[failing steps via jobs API]
  LEG --> LE[log_excerpt]
  LE -->|child run| CF[gh run view --log-failed]
  LE -->|own run / mid-run| PJ[gh run view --job id --log]
  CF --> SE[signal_excerpt: first 3 signal matches +/-3 ctx]
  PJ --> SE
  SE -->|no signal| TAIL[raw tail fallback]
  SE --> SIG[error_signature: priority-class line, normalized]
  SIG --> SEARCH[gh search issues --match body,comments]
  SEARCH -->|match| CMT[comment on root-cause issue]
  SEARCH -->|no match| TITLE[leg-title dedup -> comment or file]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
# Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing

    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do

            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then

{"content":"### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart
```
Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10089 passed, 10 skipped.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[Failed/cancelled leg] --> FS[failing steps via jobs API]
  LEG --> LE[log_excerpt]
  LE -->|child run| CF[gh run view --log-failed]
  LE -->|own run / mid-run| PJ[gh run view --job id --log]
  CF --> SE[signal_excerpt: first 3 signal matches +/-3 ctx]
  PJ --> SE
  SE -->|no signal| TAIL[raw tail fallback]
  SE --> SIG[error_signature: priority-class line, normalized]
  SIG --> SEARCH[gh search issues --match body,comments]
  SEARCH -->|match| CMT[comment on root-cause issue]
  SEARCH -->|no match| TITLE[leg-title dedup -> comment or file]
```

Done. Summary of the gh-1478 implementation:

**Changes** (all committed on `ai/gh-1478`, verified via `git log origin/main..HEAD`):

1. **`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`**
   - `signal_excerpt`: greps failed logs for `::error::` / `Message from server` / `error:` / `FAIL` / exit-code lines and quotes the first 3 matches with ±3 lines of context; raw 50-line tail only as fallback (fixes #1473 tree-noise digests).
   - Own-run/mid-run logs now resolve the failed/cancelled leg job and use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`) — the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, the root cause of #1472's empty "(no failed-step log available)" shrug.
   - Cancelled legs get a dedicated digest section: which job was in flight, its `timeout-minutes` ceiling (parsed from the workflow yaml, `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` seam), elapsed-vs-ceiling with an interpretation line.
   - Root-cause dedup: `error_signature` (priority-class line, normalized — gh log prefixes/timestamps stripped) is embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and searched via `gh search issues --match body,comments`; a match gets the digest as a comment instead of a new symptom duplicate (#1473 vs #1452 class).
   - Title dedup and auto-close-on-green behavior untouched.

2. **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — new `Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)` step in the report job: asserts the filed issue actually *quotes* the injected `::error::` line, not merely that an issue exists.

3. **`test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart`** — 13 fixture-driven shell-harness tests (tree-noise, priority order, tail fallback, cancelled section with ceiling/elapsed, signature dedup, title dedup, auto-close, inject shape, wiring).

4. **`docs/ci.md`** — testing procedure now documents the excerpt assertion and the new digest semantics.
